readout.purpose: Measured numerals only — KPI values, table figures, meter values, the brand chip. Tabular monospace.

label.purpose: Uppercase, tracked, muted — scribed captions on the instrument.

shadows.name: seat
shadows.purpose: Near-invisible rest seat on cards and selected segments — depth is carried by rules, not shadow.

shadows.name: popover
shadows.purpose: Transient floating panels and tooltips only.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Default state transition for hover/focus on controls and nav — quick and mechanical.

components.name: Default Button
components.description: The neutral control — filters, refresh, secondary actions.
components.css: .ds-btn { font: inherit; font-size: 0.9rem; padding: 0.5rem 0.9rem; border-radius: 4px; border: 1px solid rgba(30,32,36,0.14); background: #f5f4ef; color: #1e2024; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 0.12s ease, background 0.12s ease; } .ds-btn:hover { border-color: #b23122; }

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one loud control — a single confirming action (e.g. save thresholds).
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { font: inherit; font-size: 0.8rem; font-weight: 600; padding: 0.4rem 0.85rem; border-radius: 4px; border: 1px solid #b23122; background: #b23122; color: #f5f4ef; cursor: pointer; transition: filter 0.12s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { filter: brightness(1.06); }

components.name: Card
components.description: The panel face — flat, scribed hairline, squared 6px corners.
components.css: .ds-card { background: #f5f4ef; border: 1px solid rgba(30,32,36,0.14); border-radius: 6px; padding: 1.25rem 1.38rem 1.4rem; box-shadow: 0 1px 0 rgba(30,32,36,0.05); } .ds-card-h { margin: 0; font-size: 1.2rem; font-weight: 640; letter-spacing: -0.01em; color: #1e2024; }

components.name: Nav Link (active)
components.description: Selected instrument key: inset panel with a scribe-red index tick on the rail edge.
components.css: .ds-nav-active { position: relative; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; padding: 0.58rem 0.68rem 0.58rem 0.8rem; border-radius: 4px; background: #f5f4ef; color: #1e2024; font-size: 0.94rem; font-weight: 600; text-decoration: none; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(30,32,36,0.14); } .ds-nav-active::before { content: ''; position: absolute; left: 0; top: 50%; transform: translateY(-50%); width: 3px; height: 15px; border-radius: 1px; background: #b23122; }

components.name: Readout Value
components.description: The measured KPI numeral — tabular monospace, the instrument's output.
components.css: .ds-readout { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.4rem; } .ds-readout-label { font-size: 0.77rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #83857f; } .ds-readout-val { font-family: Consolas, ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', monospace; font-size: 2.25rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: -0.01em; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: #1e2024; }

components.name: Status Badge
components.description: Health pill: dot + word, tinted — color is never the sole signal.
components.css: .ds-status { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.38rem; padding: 0.15rem 0.55rem 0.15rem 0.44rem; border-radius: 999px; font-size: 0.77rem; font-weight: 600; color: #3f7a3a; background: rgba(63,122,58,0.13); border: 1px solid rgba(63,122,58,0.3); } .ds-status-dot { width: 7px; height: 7px; border-radius: 50%; background: currentColor; }

narrative.overview: The dashboard is a tradesperson's calibrated instrument bench, not a SaaS chart deck. Its job is to measure one thing — whether the after-hours phone agent earns its cost — and to report that measurement with the trustworthy, unshowy precision of a steel rule, a dial gauge, and a scribed story pole. Everything reads as satin steel and graphite: crisp hairline rules instead of floating drop shadows, squared corners instead of soft pills, and numerals set in a tabular monospace so a figure reads like an instrument's output. The world is deliberately quiet; the one warm signal in it is a single scribe-red witness mark, and it is spent sparingly. This world replaces the previous look — the generic analytics dashboard of indigo-accented, drop-shadowed KPI cards over a funnel bar chart and a table — which is the explicit anti-reference.
keyCharacteristics: Satin steel & graphite ground; one scribe-red witness accent; brass secondary.
Scribed hairline rules and crisp, squared corners — depth by line, not by shadow.
Measured numerals: readouts and data cells set in a tabular monospace.
Calm by default; the accent earns attention because it is rare.
Theme is selected (light/dark), never auto-flipped silently.

rules.name: The One Witness Rule
rules.body: Scribe-red appears on a screen only as a witness mark — the active nav tick, a focus ring, a link, or the single primary action. If two red elements compete for attention on one view, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Metals-Not-Moods Rule
rules.body: After-hours is steel-blue and business-hours is brass-amber, always, everywhere. These hues are identity, not decoration; do not recolor them per surface.

rules.name: The Measured-Numeral Rule
rules.body: Any figure a user would compare, scan a column of, or trust as a measurement is set in the readout monospace with tabular-nums. Prose figures inside sentences stay in the sans.

rules.name: The Line-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Structure is drawn with 1px scribed rules and tonal steps. If a surface needs to feel distinct, change its tone or give it a hairline — do not lift it on a shadow.

dos: Do set every measured figure in the readout monospace with tabular-nums; keep in-sentence figures in the sans.
Do convey structure and depth with 1px scribed rules and tonal layering (page → panel → recessed).
Do keep after-hours steel-blue (#2f6a92) and business-hours brass-amber (#b07a2e) fixed across every surface.
Do pair every status/health color with an icon and a word.
Do keep corners small and uniform (4px controls, 6px cards).
donts: Don't spend scribe-red on anything but a witness mark (active nav, focus, link, single primary action).
Don't reintroduce floating drop-shadow cards or the indigo SaaS-dashboard look — that is the anti-reference.
Don't use a colored border-left wider than 2px, or a shadow, to signal emphasis; use tone, rule, or type weight.
Don't use the readout monospace for prose — it is for measurement only.
Don't recolor the data pair per chart or invent a third series hue without extending this system.
